item.title: One More Week
item.description: A backpack that allows its owner to live for one week, but at the cost of someone else's life.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Urban Legend

Page Layout: Standard description, some interview

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a beaten backpack with UC, Santa Cruz, patches on it. Once opened the person opening it is slowly replaced, physically and mentally, with a young philosophy student who then returns to exploring the continental United States. He also writes about his experiences, which helps pay his way.

Central Narrative: In 1989 Charles Anton Page decided to drop out of college and explore America; he felt trapped and needed to run away. He quickly adopted a "one week at a time" philosophy, where he'd find odd jobs and beg in order to obtain enough to buy a bus ticket and some food, and then would take off on the next leg of his journey.

A year or so later, he was robbed and left for dead, and would eventually succumb to his wounds. The body was never recovered. His backpack, and the contents therein, were pawned at a local pawn shop. Someone bought the backpack, and over the next few hours was transformed into a virtual clone of Page, but without the knowledge of his death or that he was leading an extended life.

He is able to live for one week (168 hours) at a time before copies of the wounds that killed him appear on his body, and he then quickly succumbs to them. Once someone finds and opens the backpack, he is yet again allowed to live for another week, but with the usual memory lapse.

While he has adapted to the modern world somewhat (he writes a blog instead of magazine articles), he is still driven to explore the continental United States. He just does it one week at a time.

Hook/Attention Grabber: A basic urban legend about a youth cut short but still trying to find a way to accomplish his dream of exploring the United States through a mix of odd jobs, bus tickets, and hitchhiking, one week at a time.

item.title: {Seeking Greenlight} The World's Best Pizza.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Comedy, Weirdness, short and sweet

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation stumbles upon a small family-owned restaurant that happens to serve infallibly, undeniably good food.

Central Narrative: After being flagged by CHORUS, A social mapping AIC designed to detect intense spikes in mood, a small pizzeria finds itself under the attention of the Foundation. The restaurant, known as Giacomo's Pizza, makes the pretty standard claim that it serves "The World's Best." The thing is, for this bistro, that might actually be true. Anyone who tries Giacomo's pies agrees that they're the best they ever tasted -or will taste- to the point of profound satisfaction. The thing is, the foundation can't figure out why. It's just normal pizza; nothing memetic, nothing thaumaturgic, nothing chemical. In the end, when the lead researcher breaks down to the current Giacomo in charge, tearfully asking them what's so special about their pizza they merely reply "Simple. They're made with love."
Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook of the article lies in the surrealist concept of an item of food being objectively "the best." As well as the intrigue of the eyecatching associated image:

Image block within
Close and return

Additional Notes:
While this article takes on a comedic tone, I do not intend it to be a -J. Many Skips turn funny concepts into sound articles, and I want this to be one of them.

item.title: Tale 1 of Tau-13
item.description: First tale detailing the missions of MTF unit Tau-13
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre(s): Horror, Action

Page Layout: Given that this is a tale, I was going to write it like your standard narrative-driven novel. This is also the format I write most things in, save aspects of the SCP article I've drafted.

Elevator Pitch:

  • This first one will detail the team's first mission together, with flashbacks to their lives together in training.
  • The mission will involve them investigating a cult-like organization, who have been reportedly been kidnapping locals from a nearby town.
  • Upon investigation, they learn that the cult has been worshiping a horrible, Lovecraftian monster.
  • They, of course, go in for expulsion and containment.
  • They have a hard-fought battle, and through some stupid, neglectful mistakes, they lose their private to the monster.
  • Since they had all grown together in training and just as good friends, the sight of their private getting killed, combined with the psychic effects of the monstrosity, drive them very near to the edge of insanity.
  • After eventually routing out the cult, they return with broken minds. I'm thinking I'll have the Foundation use amnestics to make them forget the horrors, but deep down they still have that vastly stronger, Pavlovian-esque drive to protect each other and all innocents from these, and similar, horrors1.

Central Narrative: With the above in mind, the context is related to my SCP article currently in the Draft Critique forum. The second team that gets sent in is the team that will be written about here, and these tales will be sued to better describe their friendly relationship. This first tale in particular will describe why they are the way they are, and why they do what they do. It will describe their relationship and their drive.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I'd like to think it's unique and interesting because I will be using it, and subsequent tales, to tie all of my in-universe work together. I don't know how original this is, but I hope to add unique spins on the way character and plot development occurs.

Additional Notes: I wouldn't mind ideas on how to improve uniqueness and originality. And please, be brutally honest. If there's something you don't like, or something you do like, I'd greatly appreciate knowing what and why. Thank you in advance!

Footnotes
1. to be used for subsequent tales involving the team.

item.title: First Time Idea - No-Tell Motel
item.description: New to the site and looking to get this concept critiqued and, hopefully, greenlit.
item.content:encoded: The idea is for an SCP that is a roadside motel in the Arizona desert. This motel is a fixed point in multiple realities. The different worlds can be viewed from the different room's windows. The inside is infinitely bigger inside than outside, and labyrinthine. Examples include a barren white world of perpetual night, at the bottom of an alien ocean, an alien swamp, and etc. Creatures and other entities can break through the windows from time to time. There appears to be no staff, until those who are drawn to enter it "check out" the next day. The staffs' features can never be remembered by those that observe them. It is Euclid class, and fenced off with posted guards. Yet, still, sometimes civilians and even a guard or two, somehow, manage to enter.

item.title: Monster maker
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: There is an amusement park containing various creatures led by a British businessman, the monsters very wildly ranging from literal planet consuming monsters to sentient bug-like creatures all contained and safe for viewing, it being encouraged to observe them in their "habitats". The habitats are unusually fitted for the creature at hand with the supplies for upkeep never seen. The British businessman himself is the only one there seemingly doing everything there being everywhere in the park. The monsters at the park however were once humans. When the Businessman gets bored of the current attractions he lures people selecting three interesting individuals and giving them free items. These items slowly transform the person into one a monster before being brought in by him to display.

Central Narrative: none

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It presents the foundation with a large amount of anomalous creatures all relatively safe with the main concern being its owner and manager the buisnessman

Additional Notes: I haven't yet decided if the man will have a known identity. I'm still pondering if what to keep mystified about the man and his attractions. suggestions are very welcome.

item.title: "Now thats what I call existence"
item.description: A CD that transports listeners to a otherworldly collection.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy, Existential Happiness

Elevator Pitch: An unmarked CD that can transport any listener to a seemingly infinite hall like room. The room is covered in forms of digital media, every piece being some form of strange variation of the cd "Now that's what I call music Vol 1!".

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: SCP researchers and class D personal are transported to the collection room and are greeted by a sign that hangs off of a rail attached to the ceiling of this room that spans the full length. The sign moves into view, all that is said on the sign is "Welcome, and enjoy my collection." The Article will be split into two parts mainly, with the researchers walking down the hall and noting interesting deviations with certain items in the collection. Examples include "That's what I call actor Andy Warhol's face Vol 1!" and "That's what I call just Hoobastank Vol 1!".

The second section would detail the research teams further dives into the hall. After multiple hours of walking they come to another sign hanging from a rail, this sign precedes more of the hall but every shelf past this sign is empty. The sign proclaims that the rest of the hall is dedicated to alternate universe versions of earth that have not yet made their respective version of "That's what I call music Vol 1!". The sign then begins to wax poetic about how no matter the horrific world or terrifying problems humanity may fall under, almost every single version of humanity has had it in them to at *least* make one version of "Now that's what I call music Vol 1!". The collection is a testament to humanities capacity to at least make this one cd every time.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The foundation never actually sees the being behind the collection, and Nothing actually dangerous happens to the researchers, its just a strange walk through a weird "turtles all the way down" style museum

Additional Notes: This is my first real scp idea that I've put any weight into actually writing about and I made this post for the critique it needs but also just to make sure that this idea isn't something that has already been made. Thank you for reading


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 180 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

item.title: Axolotl
item.description: Earth’s guardian, taking the form of a massive axolotl, waiting to protect the Earth when the end of the world arrives
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A massive axolotl which lives in it’s own dimension outside of space-time . It’s regenerative abilities are so advanced, it's nearly immortal. When the end of the world comes, naturally, or in the form of an “XK end of the world scenario”, the entity will appear from its dimension to fight off the opposing force.

Central Narrative: The creature was first spotted very early in the foundation’s history. Its head was first seen coming through a wormhole leading back to its home, during one of the first XK class scenario breeches, nicknamed “Lil’ Devil”. Lil’ Devil’s body radiated immense heat, which caused drastic changes to the surrounding environment.Nearly seconds before the foundation planned to launch their final attack, the axolotl lunged from its wormhole, which it had previously moved very slowly threw, snapped at Lil’ Devil, got it in one fell swoop with no damage to the surrounding area or its self, and disappeared back threw the wormhole; leaving the foundations task force stunned. Throughout the foundation’s history, the wormhole has been spotted around the world, when the possibility of the end of the world is near, but the creature hasn’t been seen coming through the wormhole since that initial spotting, except for one education, where just the tip of the axolotls poked out of the worm hole, and completely demolished a nature reserve and multiple endangered birds in the process… That all happened after the opposing force was already naturalized. Research on the creature has been challenging because of how it never leaves its wormhole, however, they have found many carvings and paintings of the axolotl all around the world, dating back thousands of years. On multiple occasions researchers found carvings of it fighting off creatures assumed to be SCP-like entities. Some researchers think the axolotl acts out of love and fondness for humanity, having shown, despite its gigantic size, to have been very precise in how it ate Lil’ Devil, making sure any drastic movements wouldn't cause harm to civilians. Recently with more XK scenarios possible, the foundation has been hard at working on trying to make contact with the creature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I just think it’s kind of a fun and funny idea that the being which will protect Earth when the end of the world approaches, is a giant immortal axolotl, just waiting in its dimension for that time to come.

item.title: The Gate (seeking greenlights)
item.description: Creature/machine in abandoned fortress able to access other dimensions.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: History

Elevator Pitch: A creature/machine is found in an abandoned Obskurakorps laboratory and able to open up to other dimensions with a sinister past and purpose. Mostly focuses on mythology and history along with the central premise.

Central Narrative: The story is mostly told through historical documentation of an old Foundation site created post WWII. A former Obskurakorps base holding a part flesh and part mechanical entity that changes a area near it to that of another dimension. The Foundation spends years exploring these dimensions as the entity opens them though is never able to control the entity or understand how it works. It is revealed in an interview log with a captured scientist that the machine is searching for the Norse worlds of myth. Some it has found and others it continues to search for all while the potential threat of a hidden cell of the GOI remains at large.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The unknown factors that remain hidden and indecipherable all the while presenting a new threat to the foundation. The mystery that surrounds the site and the new worlds potentially within the Foundations grasp as well as the new twist it adds to a current GOI.

Additional Notes: I’d appreciate any feedback on tips to progress my article through the sites greenlighting process as this is still pretty new to me and I’d like to get it right.

item.title: A recursive Zip Archive.
item.description: A ZIP file that contains an exact copy of itself. This is a real thing.
item.content:encoded:
I don't know if real things qualify for SCP articles but there is this thing called a recursive zip file aka a "quine". Link here: https://research.swtch.com/zip

What makes this remind me of an anomalious SCP is the fact that when you open a quine zip file, you find an exact copy of itself inside. Extracting the contents will reveal an identical copy of the zip file you just extracted. Extracting that one will reveal yet another one. Round and round we go.

To make a more SCPish analogy, think of a box that contains another box the same size. And inside this box is another box of the same size as well. And so on and so forth.

So what we have is basically a zip file that seemingly pulls data out of thin air. The link contains example files to see for yourself.

What do you think?

item.title: A 4th degree burn
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Normal scp page layout

Elevator Pitch: Keter level scp, when humans sustain burns of incredibly high temperatures, their nervous systems re-wire to survive in intense heat. They turn into vaguely humanoid personages of flame who can't talk and can only live in intense heat.

Central Narrative: Instances of this scp are rare, due to level's of heat required to create this scp
rarely occur on earth. The narrative would follow the foundation containing several instances of this scp after a failed rocket launch in South Korea. After losing several instances due to decreasing temperatures, they are able to create a containment chamber with a increased temperature so then the final instance could be contained. Examination shows that a modified version of the nervous system is intact, and interviews show that the instances can "feel", as if they still had a body. Communicating is done through manipulating the flame into short words, although they describe this process as "Painful." The foundation can recreate this and they roast a D-class and make another instance. They then cool down the chamber and discover the temperature they "die" at.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: Similar to other skips, instances hate their predicament, but the foundation refuses to let them die so then they can contain the anomaly. The foundation in cold, y'all. Basically it's the fear of literally burning forever. A literal hell.

Additional Notes: I don't know the exact temperature the conversion takes place yet, i'll do some research later.

item.title: Idea: SCP - Napoleon Bonaparte's Ghost
item.description: This SCP will be a coffeepot that contains the ghost of Napoleon Bonaparte.
item.content:encoded: So I had this idea for an item SCP that, when poured out, causes the ghost of Napoleon Bonaparte to pour out. This ghost will have a relentless drive to "bring back French glory" and will continuously demand the Foundation to help him be reinstalled as the Emperor of France, of course mostly to no avail.
